contribution.position: I hold my earlier position and answer product's claim that 'on reliability, nobody else sees a problem, so I would treat it as settled.' That is directly contradicted by artifact:incident-log, which product's turn never addresses: a 1.8% 30-day error rate against a 0.3% SLO with two sev2 incidents means the error budget is already exhausted before this change lands. QA's artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed) and the artifact:perf-report (p99 within budget) validate the change in isolation, not the live service it will deploy into; ops's artifact:ops-runbook covers rollback mechanics but rollback does not restore a burned error budget or resolve attribution ambiguity during an active SLO breach. I also flag an evidence gap: no artifact in the list shows post-incident remediation status, error-budget recovery, or a current-period error rate trending back toward the 0.3% SLO — the transcript's 'reliability is settled' framing rests on the absence of such data, not on its presence. Until the incident log shows recovery or a new artifact demonstrates it, the reliability axis remains opposed to absorbing new change this week.
